title: Pakistan's interior minister says social media and streaming platforms will have to register with a new regulator
date_note: Arab News is dated 24 November; the page gives no earlier day for the announcement.
geo_basis: government announcement at a seminar in Islamabad, as the article states
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said at an Islamabad seminar that social media companies will have to register with the Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority and name representatives who can deal with Pakistani authorities, Arab News reports. Registration would also cover streaming services and major content creators. Naqvi said platforms act on only 47% of requests from Pakistan's counterterrorism departments, and that blocking a whole platform would remain a last resort.
plain: Pakistan's interior minister says social media and streaming platforms must register with a regulator. He says platforms act on only 47% of the counterterrorism departments' requests.
exec: Platforms operating in Pakistan may face mandatory registration; Arab News gives no deadline.

evidence.quote: Only 47% of the requests made by us, by our counter terrorism departments, are acted upon by social media platforms

validation.note: Only Arab News read; Samaa returned 403. Statements are the minister's as Arab News relays them.

review.note: Title, date, 47% quote, authority, scope compared with Arab News; single source stands
